weeks.crew: Scott/Gerald and Zane (Mon); Scott/Gerald, Ben/Zane, rotating (Tue–Thu)

days.work: Install last 2 poles, move equipment back
details: Install last 2 poles at the park
Replace old HID fixtures (metal halide/HPS) on existing poles with new LED luminaires
Remove old luminaire and ballast wiring
Install new LED luminaire in same mounting position
Run new harness or adapt existing wiring
Connect new LED driver in ECE
Verify aim matches Field Aiming Diagram

items: Musco's "5 Easy Pieces" are: foundation, pole, ECE, structural/harness, luminaire — the contactor cabinet is NOT one of the 5, it's a separate add-on
Full install is 6 steps: foundation → pole sections → ECE → contactor cabinet (separate enclosure at base) → harness → luminaire
Contactor cabinet is a separate enclosure at the pole base — NOT inside the ECE. It houses the main contactor, control transformer, and incoming power feed
Weld marks must align when slip-fitting pole sections
Come-along straps seat the sections — you'll handle rigging on the ground
Handhole at the base — where conduit enters and supply wiring comes in
HID components: ballast, capacitor, ignitor vs LED components: driver, fuse
ECE layout — where drivers live, where fuses are, where the ground bar is
Wire harness connects ECE to poletop — on retrofits this often gets replaced
Field Aiming Diagram concept — every luminaire has a labeled position

tools: Non-contact voltage tester — always verify everything
Fish tape — likely needed on retrofit wiring runs
1000V megger/megohmmeter — required for harness insulation testing (Musco procedure)
OOA (Off-Off-Auto) switch key — for CMC radio replacement
Torx T25 screwdriver — for radio bracket screws in CMC
Channel locks or pliers — for antenna replacement on CMC
safety: LOTO (Lockout/Tagout) — know the procedure, ask the journeyman before touching any energized equipment
Bucket truck awareness — stay clear of swing radius, never walk under a raised bucket
Arc flash — ECE enclosures can be energized, treat everything as live until proven otherwise
3-point contact on any ladder or climbing
dayOneTips: Gear ready: hardhat, safety glasses, sunscreen applied, gaiter, water jug full
Watch what the journeyman does before touching anything — every crew has their flow
Ask "what do you need next?" constantly — a good helper anticipates the next tool or material
Never walk away without telling someone — on a pole job people need to know where you are
When in doubt ask — "should I seal this conduit now?" shows you know what needs to happen
impressTheCrew: Already knowing what a Field Aiming Diagram is
Knowing the difference between a driver and a ballast
Handing the right wrench (9/16") before being asked
Having duct seal ready when the conduit goes in
Keeping the work area clean and organized — especially at the base of the pole

cheatSheet.meaning: Electrical Components Enclosure — the box on the pole (fuses, drivers, disconnect, ground bar)
Located bottom-right of ECE. Rotate 90° CCW = OFF, 90° CW = ON. Top = line side, bottom = load side
Splits power from disconnect to fuses. Can be A/B/C (3-phase), A/B (phase-to-phase), or A/B/N (phase-to-neutral)
Swapping HID fixtures for LED on existing poles
Factory wiring from ECE to fixtures at top
Driver power in — black, green, blue/white stripe wires
Driver power out — red and black wires
Plugs into driver face — green, yellow, black, red wires. If unplugged, driver may not be controllable
Map showing where each pole and fixture goes
LED power supply (replaces ballast). Has 3 LED status lights on its face
Label like A1, B2 — matches all components
Separate enclosure at pole base housing main contactor(s), control transformer, and incoming power feed — NOT inside the ECE
Powerline Communication — system that sends control signals over the high-voltage lighting bus. Master PLC in the cabinet, remote PLC at each pole
Control & Monitoring Cabinet — central control cabinet with communication radio, control modules, and monitoring equipment
Musco's remote control/monitoring system — call 877-347-3319 for tech support
Exothermic weld for grounding connections (Arlye's work)
